index_warning: Supplied segment header says 34:36-48; the body is al-Ahzab 33:36-48.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet’s marriage to Zaynab, despite public opposition, would remove a wrong custom and an unnatural restriction.
rows.anchor: Finally, the Almighty bade him to marry disregarding any opposition from people so that this step could eradicate a wrong custom and an unnatural restriction

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi presents his account as the incident’s real form, reached after critically evaluating the narratives.
rows.anchor: Described above is the real form of the incident that I have gauged after critically evaluating all the narratives.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Orientalists gave the incident a distorted and sinister presentation through exaggeration and fabrication.
rows.anchor: Orientalists have given it a very evil shape because of their exaggerations and fabrications

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He says Orientalists drew these misrepresentations from Muslim tafsīr and sīrah works.
rows.anchor: they have gathered the content of these misrepresentations from the tafsīr and sīrah works of Muslim authors.

index_warning: Supplied segment header says 34:36-48; the body is al-Ahzab 33:36-48.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Verse 36 introduces the incident narrated in the following verses.
rows.anchor: This verse serves as a prelude to the incident coming up in the succeeding verses.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse states a general principle, rather than a rule limited to Zayd and Zaynab’s case.
rows.anchor: What is said here is not merely related to Zayd (rta) and Zaynab (rta). It is a statement of a general principle.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The principle rests on the earlier statement that the Prophet’s right over believers exceeds their rights over one another.
rows.anchor: and the right of the Prophet is greater on the believers than they have on one another

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When God and His Messenger decide a matter, believing men and women have no grounds for hesitation.
rows.anchor: then there is no room for any hesitancy for believing men and women.

index_warning: Supplied segment header says 34:36-48; the body is al-Ahzab 33:36-48.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A Messenger’s decisions are made with God’s permission, so believers must obey absolutely and may not object or disobey.
rows.anchor: decisions taken by a messenger of God is with His permission; Hence, the messenger must be obeyed in the absolute sense.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This injunction applies when the Prophet has issued a clearly explicit directive; some of his statements were suggestions.
rows.anchor: this injunction relates to the situation when it is clearly known that the Prophet has given an explicit directive.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When Companions recognized a statement as the Prophet’s own suggestion rather than God’s directive, they could offer counter-suggestions, which he sometimes accepted.
rows.anchor: they presented their own counter suggestions as well and at times they were even accepted by him.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zaynab first understood the Prophet’s proposal that she marry Zayd as a suggestion; once she learned it was his wish, she accepted.
rows.anchor: Later, when she came to know that this was the Prophet’s wish that this marriage take place, she accepted the proposal.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After Zayd’s divorce, Zaynab likewise treated the Prophet’s proposal as a suggestion and sought istikhārah before accepting.
rows.anchor: Thereupon she had replied that she will not take a decision without doing istikhārah.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zayd viewed the request not to divorce as advice, believing the final decision remained his; he divorced when the marriage proved unworkable.
rows.anchor: the final decision lies with him in this matter.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi reads the verse as a general principle whose revelation was occasioned by the circumstances of Zayd and Zaynab.
rows.anchor: In my opinion, what is mentioned in the verse is a general principle whose revelation had been occasioned by the circumstances.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Defying a Prophet’s directive is impermissible in every circumstance, contradicts faith, and leads into error.
rows.anchor: it is not permissible for believing men and women to defy a directive of the Prophet (sws) in any circumstances.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The principle is directed especially at the sūrah’s Hypocrites: they must obey completely or face the consequences.
rows.anchor: Hypocrite men and women whose attitude is under discussion since the very beginning of this sūrah so that they get around to obey him completely.

index_warning: Supplied segment header says 34:36-48; the body is al-Ahzab 33:36-48.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hypocrites tried to diminish Zayd before people by labeling him a slave as part of their malicious campaign.
rows.anchor: Hypocrite men and women tried their best to belittle him in the eyes of people by labeling him a slave

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zayd’s patience under humiliation was rewarded by God’s naming him as favored; this recognition outshone any other accolade.
rows.anchor: It was a result of this patience that God rewarded him by mentioning him with this attribute.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi says all human blessings come from God.
rows.anchor: Whatever a person gets is from God.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zayd’s case resembled Joseph’s: he was captured in a raid, probably enslaved by a Christian and sold, then brought by God’s plan to the Prophet, opening religious and worldly blessings.
rows.anchor: his case was similar to that of Joseph (sws). He was imprisoned in a plunder raid and probably remained the slave of a Christian

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet’s affection brought Zayd Islam, adoption-like status, freedom, and marriage to the Prophet’s cousin; entering the Prophet’s household was the highest family honor.
rows.anchor: The Prophet (sws) liberated him from slavery and wedded him to his cousin sister.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording wa-idh taqūlu indicates that the Prophet repeatedly asked Zayd to keep his wife and fear God.
rows.anchor: the Prophet (sws) must have repeatedly requested Zayd (rta) to not divorce Zaynab (rta) and fear God.

index_warning: Supplied segment header says 34:36-48; the body is al-Ahzab 33:36-48.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording implies Zayd repeatedly expressed an intention to divorce and was stopped by the Prophet each time.
rows.anchor: Zayd (rta) must have expressed his intention many times before the Prophet (sws) and each time he was stopped by him

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to fear God shows the Prophet emphatically opposed Zayd’s proposed step.
rows.anchor: the Prophet (sws) must have said the words to emphatically stop Zayd (rta) and did not find it appropriate for him to take this step.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When asked whether Zaynab had done something to prompt divorce, Zayd emphatically said no.
rows.anchor: he had emphatically replied in the negative.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zayd’s only stated grievance was that Zaynab’s noble lineage made her feel superior to him.
rows.anchor: because of her noble lineage she has a sense of superiority over me

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi says that complaint did not justify divorce and may reflect Zayd’s sensitivity more than Zaynab’s arrogance, against the background of Hypocrite propaganda.
rows.anchor: This could be because of Zayd’s (rta) own over sensitivity than that of Zaynab’s (rta) air of superiority

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zayd felt Zaynab was being targeted and mocked because of him, and thought divorce would spare her the critics’ attacks.
rows.anchor: The only remedy to this is to divorce her and provide her solace from the sharp tongues of the critics.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sentence is a circumstantial clause: while telling Zayd to keep his wife and fear God, the Prophet was concealing what God would reveal.
rows.anchor: grammatically in the category of state ( hāl) ie.: when you were telling Zayd not to divorce his wife and fear God

rows.speaker: Ibn Kathīr
rows.claim: Ibn Kathīr says the narratives cited by some exegetes are baseless and should be omitted.
rows.anchor: In this regard, Ibn Kathīr has very rightly said:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi agrees with Ibn Kathīr and regards even citing these narratives for refutation as sinful.
rows.anchor: I agree with this comment. I regard it to be a sin to cite them even for the purpose of refutation.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He condemns al-Ṭabarī for citing narratives without sufficient caution.
rows.anchor: May God forgive Ibn Jarīr al-Ṭabarī. He does not exercise caution in citing narratives.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the Prophet had initiated the marriage to elevate the status of slaves, he deeply wanted it to succeed and tried emphatically to prevent divorce.
rows.anchor: Since the Prophet (sws) was instrumental for this marriage because he wanted to raise the status of slaves, it was his deep desire that it should succeed.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet expected divorce to burden Zaynab twice: first with her enemies’ criticism, then with the stigma of divorce from a freed slave; marrying her himself would console her.
rows.anchor: Zaynab (rta) will doubly feel its brunt: she bore the censuring of her enemies

index_warning: Supplied segment header says 34:36-48; the body is al-Ahzab 33:36-48.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet feared Hypocrite propaganda accusing him of marrying his adopted son’s former wife, so he wanted the divorce not to occur; God intended it to reform a jāhili custom through the Prophet and teach messengers to face criticism.
rows.anchor: God wanted that it does take place so that through the hands of the Prophet (sws) a wrong custom of the jāhiliyyah period be reformed.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This principle is linked to verses 1–3 and 7 and developed in verses 38–39: fear of people and interests obstructs religious commitment.
rows.anchor: The greatest impediment in the way of adhering to the precepts of religion is fear of people and interests.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God charges His messengers to fear Him alone in religious matters and give no regard to others.
rows.anchor: the Almighty has imposed this responsibility on His messengers that in matters of religion they should fear God and give regard to no one except Him.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Messengers braved great danger to carry out this duty, leaving an example for later people who serve religion.
rows.anchor: the whole history of God’s messengers bears witness that they braved the storms of this path and faced the greatest of dangers to discharge this responsibility.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After Zayd fully ended the relationship, God arranged to disclose the Prophet’s concealed wish and married him to Zaynab to remove the adopted-son marriage restriction.
rows.anchor: the Almighty made arrangements to reveal the secret the Prophet (sws) harboured in his heart

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word watar means need or requirement and carries an associated sense of relationship because people become associated with what they need.
rows.anchor: means “need” and “requirement.” From here the meaning of relationship and association is incorporated in it.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase about Zayd ending his need means he completely severed his relationship with Zaynab; using it instead of divorce includes completion of the waiting period.
rows.anchor: The benefit of using this word instead of the word divorce

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording “We wedded her to you” implies the Prophet hesitated over public comments but married Zaynab at God’s directive.
rows.anchor: It is evident from this that the Prophet (sws) undertook this marriage at God’s behest.
